content.text: A $15 set of resistance bands can do almost everything a rack of dumbbells can — and it fits in a drawer. Here's a complete full-body routine you can do in your living room, a hotel room, or a park, in about 20 minutes.

items: Constant tension — unlike dumbbells, bands load your muscles through the entire range of motion
Joint-friendly — great for anyone easing back into training or managing joint pain
Packable — the entire kit weighs less than a pair of sneakers
Scalable — 5 resistance levels means beginners and advanced lifters use the same set

content.text: Do 2–3 rounds of the circuit below. Rest 30–60 seconds between exercises, and rest 1–2 minutes between rounds.

items: Band Squats — 15 reps (stand on band, handles at shoulders)
Band Rows — 15 reps (anchor band to a door, pull to ribs)
Band Chest Press — 12 reps per side (anchor behind you, press forward)
Band Deadlifts — 15 reps (stand on band, hinge at hips)
Band Overhead Press — 12 reps (stand on band, press up)
Band Glute Bridges — 15 reps (band above knees)
Slow down the eccentric (lowering) phase — this is where bands build the most strength
Move up a band level once 3 rounds feels easy, don't just add more reps
Anchor bands at door height for presses, floor height for rows to hit the right angle

items.question: Can resistance bands really build muscle like weights?
items.answer: Yes. Studies comparing resistance band training to free weights show similar strength and muscle gains when training is taken close to failure. The key is progressive overload — moving to a heavier band as you get stronger, just like adding weight to a dumbbell.

items.question: How often should I do a resistance band full-body workout?
items.answer: 3 times per week with a rest day in between is ideal for most people. This gives your muscles time to recover while still building consistent strength over a few weeks.
